text:
Sam: Heads-up: console folks want to show "effective routing" + "granted role" on the route detail panel. Problem: for quota-aware routing we sometimes apply a transient fallback role (quota-shield). How do we surface this without confusing customers?
Priya: We should show two things: the evaluated role and the effective role used for billing/limits. Label them clearly: Evaluated role = what authz matched; Applied role = what routing actually used.
Diego: +1. From API perspective we can return `evaluated_role` and `applied_role` in the permission metadata. But note: applied_role might be a synthetic role (quota-shield) that doesn't exist in org config. Need an id and a human-friendly label.
Marta: UX: don't expose synthetic internal IDs to users. Show a small badge "(quota-shield)" and a tooltip that explains why. Also include the sample group if this was a canary or staged rollout.
Sam: Telemetry question: ops wants to know how often quota-shield triggers per route and per customer. We need an event with `route`, `decision_path` (list), `applied_role`, and `sample_group`. Sampling strategy? We shouldn't emit every single request.
Priya: For metrics, aggregate on the service side and send counters. Emit a counter `perm.applied_role.count` with tags route, applied_role, decision (allow/deny/fallback), and sample_group. For traces, tag one span with `rbac.applied_role` and `rbac.decision_path_hash` so we can find representative traces.
Diego: Implementation detail: decision_path might be long (multiple fallbacks). Instead of sending full list in telemetry, send a stable hash plus a short human reason like `quota_exceeded` or `no_affinity`. For the API header used by console, a short array of steps is fine but must be size-limited.
Marta: Privacy/Security: console should not call the authz API on behalf of other tenants. The metadata header must be returned only when the downstream request is in the same tenant context and console session has permission. Also, for Dedicated customers, default off unless explicitly enabled via tenant config.
Sam: Example small header payload (base64 JSON) we discussed: ```{ "evaluated_role": "writer-v2", "applied_role": "quota-shield-low-priority", "applied_label": "Low-priority (quota shield)", "reason": "quota_exceeded", "sample_group": "staged-A" }```
Priya: Make sure header naming is consistent with other infra: `X-RW-Perm-Info`. Add `preview=true` flag when the console is using the preview endpoint.
Diego: Proxy limits: nginx default header size can choke; keep header < 1.5KB. Also ensure we gracefully degrade: if header can't be added, log `perm.meta_missing` metric with reason `header_too_big` or `downstream_reject`.
Marta: Console microcopy proposal: show "Effective role: Low-priority (quota shield)" and under it a muted line "Evaluated as writer-v2 — reason: quota_exceeded — sample: staged-A" with a link "Learn why" to rollout docs. For synthetic roles link to a short explain page not the entitlement editor.
Sam: Rollout plan: 1) Diego to change authz API to accept `perm_info=1` and optionally return `X-RW-Perm-Info`, 2) Priya to add metric counters and span tags, 3) Marta to prototype UI copy + tooltip, 4) Sam to add config toggle for Dedicated/Private tenants.
Diego: I'll include an idempotent feature guard and make default off for tenant types other than Hosted. Also will add a server-side rate limiter so we don't leak too many headers under high qps.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: authz-v2 2026-05-02T02:00Z  canary=5% owner=@Diego
Sam: ok team, let's reconvene after Diego's draft PR. Thanks!
